text:
Sam Patel: Heads up — customer (AcroPay) escalated. After yesterday's OpenAPI update customers using generated SDKs (TS/Go/Python) are getting auth failures (401) and a couple of 422s. Hosted API works in curl.

Sam Patel: Quick repro I ran locally: 
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-example
2) cd sdk-example && npm i @redwood/sdk@0.9.0
3) npx openapi-generator-cli generate -i openapi.yaml -g typescript-fetch -o out/sdk-ts
4) node out/sdk-ts/demo.js --key="ACTUAL_KEY"

Result: 401, body: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"Missing credentials"} even though same key with curl works.

Nina Gomez: I reproduced. Root cause looks like header name drift — openapi.yaml now emits an apiKey named `X-Api-Key` in the securitySchemes while our older generator config expected `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Some generated clients put the key in `Authorization` and some put it in `x-api-key` (lowercase) causing mismatch on our side-surface layer which canonicalizes header names.

Matt Li: stack trace from typescript client when running demo: 
```
Error: Request failed with status code 401
 at createError (node_modules/axios/lib/core/createError.js:16:15)
 at settle (node_modules/axios/lib/core/settle.js:17:12)
 at IncomingMessage.handleStreamEnd (node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:269:11)
```
Also saw this log in our gateway: `WARN auth: header not found: Authorization`

Dev Support Bot: Created ticket INC-2345 for AcroPay, priority=P1, linked to this thread :ticket: 

Lee Wong: This is definitely CI drift — openapi.yaml changed in the product repo but devex SDK regen pipeline didn't trigger because our checksum matcher ignores `components/securitySchemes` changes (bug). We need a guard that fails SDK CI when the generated client diff isn't empty.

Ana Rodriguez: Short-term mitigation: pin the generator config to the previous behavior and cut patch releases for SDKs. Medium-term: add a smoke test in SDK CI that actually sends a minimal auth test against sandbox to detect header name regressions. Also add an explicit changelog entry when securitySchemes change.

Sam Patel: Another wrinkle: some SDKs are retrying idempotent writes but not sending idempotency-key header, so customer observed duplicate charges on retry (billing incident). Example call was a POST /invoices that got a 502 then a retry — second POST accepted. We need to ensure generated clients include an idempotency middleware or make it obvious in examples.

Nina Gomez: Agreed. Action items: 
- regen TS/Python/Go clients with corrected header mapping (Nina + Matt)
- cut patch releases (0.9.3 for TS, 0.9.2 for Python) (Matt)
- add integration auth smoke test to SDK CI (Lee)
- update regen pipeline to fail on any generated diff and open PR automatically (Ana)
- update public changelog and internal release notes (Sam)

Matt Li: I'll take regen + patch release. Will also add a test that asserts `Authorization` header presence when security scheme is bearer, and `X-Api-Key` when apiKey scheme is used. Will push PR in the next 2 hours.

Sam Patel: Customer is on Dedicated and asking for a hotfix today — can you also DM Amelia in support once patch is tagged so they can validate?

Matt Li: :thumbsup: will tag patch release and DM Amelia. I’ll include repro steps and a temporary support branch link.

Ana Rodriguez: Also going to add an item to release checklist: "validate SDK auth headers against openapi securitySchemes" and a note to coordinate with platform when changing securitySchemes.

Sam Patel: Thanks everyone. Let's keep this thread updated with PR links and release numbers.
